reason: Reproduced exactly, at both widths, on the plainest path. Driven at 390x844 and 768x1024: open owner-editing, press 'Move a week later', press Escape (Done) - or simply press Delete, which closes the editor by itself. The editor is then closed and the bar is filled: data-editor-open is absent, data-undo="true", .b-undo computes position:fixed (390: rect 12,754.6 366x77.4, band 755-844 with its 12px inset; 768: 958-1024). The two guards that give a fixed object its band are both scoped to the sheet - b.css:1322 [data-editor-open] { scroll-padding-bottom: var(--b-sheet,30px) } and b.css:1326 [data-medium] .b-field[data-editor-open] { padding-bottom: ... } - so measured with the panel closed the field's padding-bottom is 28px at 390 and 56px at 768 and the scroll root's scroll-padding-bottom computes 'auto'. The finding's numbers are right to the pixel. Harm, measured, two kinds. (1) Focus parking: from the top of the document with the bar filled and no editor, the 4th Tab lands on 'Edit Venue walk-through' and the browser parks it at top 800 bottom 828 against a bar top of 755 - fully covered, and elementFromPoint at its centre returns .b-undo. The same happens at 768 (control 996-1024 against a bar at 958-1012, centre resolves to .b-undo) and again later in the same cycle on 'Edit Menu tasting at The Orchard' (390: 798-826, occluded). A keyboard or switch owner has focus on a control they cannot see, and the pixels they can see there belong to Undo, so the obvious tap fires the wrong thing. (2) Stranded content: scrolled to the true document end at 390 the whole footer - 'Kept by Orla', 'Updated 15 July 2026', 'Signal Timeline', rect 760-816 - sits under a bar whose top is 755, with zero scroll left to free it. The provenance line, the one thing that says whose plan this is, is unreachable. The bar is not a toast: paintUndo (render-b.js:515) has no timer, and the bar was still filled and 77px tall 12 seconds after a delete. This is the named class at lessons.md:83, 'Floating objects erase what is under them - a dock, drawer, or pill gets its band reserved in real layout', creeping back on the one floating object that was never covered. It does not restate a gate: interaction-check.mjs:1889-1906 asserts 'nothing parks under the sheet' with the test literally scoped to at.closest('.b-edit'), and interaction-check.mjs:995-1015 asserts the reserve and the stranded-row check only against .b-edit with the panel open. Both pass and neither can see this. The fix is CSS plus four lines of JS that mirror an existing writer; it touches no colour, no weight, no architecture, and it is not the round-7 refusal to move the editor's band to the foot - it gives the bar a band it has never had.
sharpenedFix: Mirror the sheet's mechanism rather than falling back to it. (a) In the max-width:1023px block widen both guards: [data-editor-open], [data-undo="true"] { scroll-padding-bottom: max(var(--b-sheet, 0px), var(--b-undo, 0px), 30px); } and [data-medium] .b-field[data-editor-open], [data-medium] .b-field[data-undo="true"] { padding-bottom: max(var(--b-sheet, 0px), var(--b-undo, 0px), var(--gap-block)); }. Use max(), not var(--b-sheet, var(--b-undo)) as proposed: the two states co-exist (bar filled with the editor open) and a fallback chain would silently drop whichever is larger. (b) In paintUndo(), after setting data-undo, write root.style.setProperty('--b-undo', (bar.offsetHeight + 24) + 'px') when getComputedStyle(bar).position === 'fixed', and root.style.removeProperty('--b-undo') on the empty branch beside root.removeAttribute('data-undo') - the exact shape openEditor/closeEditor already use for --b-sheet. Because the bar wraps to two lines at 390 (77px) and one at 768 (54px), it must be measured, not guessed. (c) While in this rule, fix the shortfall the same measurement exposes: b.css:1335 raises the sheet to bottom:76px whenever the bar is filled, but openEditor still writes --b-sheet as offsetHeight + 24, so with the bar filled at 390 and 768 the field reserves 583px against a covered band of 635px - 52px short. Write --b-sheet from window.innerHeight - node.getBoundingClientRect().top + 24 so it follows the sheet's actual top rather than assuming an inset. (d) Assert it in the gate: with the panel closed and the bar filled, at 390 and 768, Tab through every .b-grab and require elementFromPoint at each focused control's centre to resolve inside that control, and at maximum scroll require .b-foot's bottom to sit above the bar's top.
